# FEIB05 results

All logarithms are base 2. H, A, B, Gamma and P are measured in bits. I is total influence; ratios are bits per unit of excess influence I−1. Every reported record was computed with integer Walsh and restriction numerators and recomputed independently. Only logarithms and their weighted sums use floating point.

Input x is the integer sum of x_i 2^i. Bit x of a hexadecimal truth table is 1 exactly when f(x)=−1. Leading zeros are retained to specify 2^n bits. A negative output is the TRUE output of a named Boolean property. Input coordinate i is bit i of x. The tables directory contains complete hexadecimal truth tables, including the long 18-variable one.

## K33 record and the wording correction

The host accepts an edge set that CONTAINS a perfect matching; accepting only edge sets that are exactly a matching does not give this construction. With edge p=3r+c, let cross(p) contain every edge in row r or column c. At core inputs cross(p) and cross(p) without p, output the fresh coin y_p; otherwise output whether a perfect matching is contained. The nine pairs are disjoint. This is balanced.

The host accepts 247 of 512 core inputs. Nine coins occupy 18 additional core inputs. A second construction using Hall’s condition agreed at every one of the 262144 inputs; see [construction certificate](k33_construction_certificate.json). The table SHA in that file uses packed little-endian truth-table bytes, not an unspecified external serialization.

I = 261/128 = 2.039062500000; I−1 = 133/128. H/(I−1) = 6.521845710923046576. H/I = 3.323392641965; the quoted record uses the former ratio.

| component | bits | component/(I−1) |
|---|---:|---:|
| H | 6.776605309006 | 6.521845710923 |
| A | 4.361829264436 | 4.197850720660 |
| B | 2.414776044570 | 2.323994990263 |
| Gamma | 0.065424559676 | 0.062964989763 |
| P | 2.283875991917 | 2.198015992221 |

A supplies 64.365992% of H; B supplies 35.634008%. The Gamma contribution is small. The largest B contributions come from Fourier levels 1, 2 and 3 (see the table below). The record is carried primarily by containment A, not large sign cancellation. Gamma is part of the decomposition of B and must not be added again to H.

## Best ratios found by dimension

These are heuristic search lower bounds, not certified maxima. Functions on n inputs may ignore some inputs; the next table gives essential dimensions. Records from smaller dimensions are inherited as candidates in larger dimensions. Each column optimizes its own function.

| n | max found A/(I−1) | max found B/(I−1) | max found Gamma/(I−1) | max found H/(I−1) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 | 4.173533749351 | 2.262756797677 | 0.729836051872 | 6.347067498702 |
| 7 | 4.173533749351 | 2.345867735805 | 0.783215259430 | 6.347067498702 |
| 8 | 4.173533749351 | 2.430158924052 | 0.828442340816 | 6.363969446288 |
| 9 | 4.173533749351 | 2.573953469707 | 0.862066394750 | 6.429941892810 |
| 10 | 4.173533749351 | 2.618025428958 | 0.895788073140 | 6.457041884365 |
| 11 | 4.173533749351 | 2.618025428958 | 0.923140455968 | 6.457041884365 |
| 12 | 4.173533749351 | 2.618025428958 | 0.923140455968 | 6.457041884365 |

The explicit six-input B witness is `0x00eceeee00ae8eee`, with B/(I−1) = 2.262756797677, B = 1.697067598258 bits and I = 1.750000000000. This exceeds both 2.26 and the sharper threshold (6.521845710923048−2)/2 = 2.260922855462 forced by Theorem 1.

The largest B ratio found is 2.618025428958 at n=10 (essential dimension 10); B=3.190718491542 bits, I=2.218750000000. Complete table: [tables/search_n10_B.hex](tables/search_n10_B.hex). The integer certificate is [certificates/search_n10_B.npz](certificates/search_n10_B.npz). Its full truth table is `0xfefefefefffefe68feaafea8feeafc80fefeccc8fefacc80feaac880feaacc00fefefee8fef8f880fea8e880f880f000fee8c880f8f080000000000000000000fefefeeefefafc00feaafeaafeaafc00fefeccccfefacc00eeaacc88eeaacc00fefefeeef0f0f000feaafeaaf0a0f000fefeccccf0f0c0000000000000000000`.

The A records in the searched range plateau; B rises across the smaller dimensions and then plateaus in this run. This is compatible with bounded ratios but supplies no upper bound: the range is small, and failure to improve is an optimization limitation. The K33 example at n=18 has A/(I−1)=4.197850720660, already above the search plateau. Neither supremum is settled.

The B winner has a coordinate with positive and negative directed differences, so it is not unate. This rules out equivalence under input/output signs and permutations to monotone AND, tribes, majority, recursive majority, and the monotone K33 coin record. It was found by perturbing K33-derived candidates; no known exact name is identified here. Non-unateness alone does not classify it or establish novelty. Its exact directed-edge counts and a comparison with the coordinate-fixed K33 completion family are in [characterization.json](characterization.json).

## Totals for known families and all search winners

Standard disjoint tribes are generally unbalanced. Ratios involving I−1 are only compared for balanced functions. The five-input table 0x00aaeeee ignores coordinate 2; removing that coordinate gives the actual four-input record 0x0aee. The five-input B census record 0x008eeeee has B/(I−1)=2.153759374820.

AND_n is TRUE only at the all-ones input. Tribes_bxw is OR of b disjoint w-input ANDs. majority_n is strict majority for odd n. address_k uses k low input bits to select one of the following 2^k data inputs. Recursive majority of 3 at depth 2 is majority of three disjoint majority-of-3 gates. known_coin8 is the six-input host 0xf005f0f0fdfdf with independent multiplicative coin flips at core inputs 12 and 39.

## Level-by-level contributions

These are sums over sets of size k, without conditioning on the level. Thus each numeric column sums to the corresponding total above; mass sums to 1. All omitted levels have exactly zero Fourier mass. The complete table including zero levels is [levels.csv](levels.csv). Sources: structured.json, verified_structured.json and best.json.

## Exact certificates and independent checks

For each table, certificates/<name>.npz stores integer walsh_numerators w_S=2^n fhat(S), upper_mass_numerators sum_{U⊇S}w_U², abs1_numerators=2^n abs1(S), restriction_nonzero_counts, and denominator=2^(2n). Restriction statistics are filled on the nonzero Fourier support; zero-Fourier-weight terms never contribute.

score.py computes mixed differences directly in the input domain. verify_independent.py instead forms each restriction coefficient from the inverse Walsh transform of the Fourier supersets. It checks divisibility of every integer restriction numerator and a separate Parseval identity for every nonzero coefficient. Total influence is checked a second way by counting disagreeing cube edges. verify_records.py compares all six quantities, including every level, between the two scripts for every search winner. Logs and exact source files are retained.

Headline scores were also recomputed with 60-digit Decimal logarithms in [high_precision.json](high_precision.json). K33 gives H/(I−1)=6.521845710923046575658143972949; the B winner gives B/(I−1)=2.618025428957766259992985612521. These are high-precision numerical evaluations of exact integer data, not formal interval enclosures.

## Search and limitations

Balanced single swaps choose one positive and one negative input. Integer spectra are updated exactly; A, B and H are rescored from integer squared coefficients and a superset zeta transform. For Gamma, an integer ternary table of mixed differences and its absolute-value sums are updated exactly after each flip. Rejected moves are undone. A periodic annealing schedule and restarts explore different basins. Later passes lower the temperature, inherit smaller winners, and try shared and independent coin-site extensions.

search_initial.cpp, search.cpp, search_polish.cpp preserve the engine versions used by the saved passes. Seeds and proposal counts are fixed in run_search.py, refine.py, final_search.py and polish.py; the JSONL records include run seeds and checkpoints. layouts.cpp additionally enumerates every coordinate-fixed balanced K33 completion with zero through three coins and is not a general exhaustive Boolean-function search.

No claim of exhaustive optimization for n≥6 is made. A plateau with dummy coordinates is a valid lower bound on the larger cube but does not demonstrate a new essential-variable record. The broad conjectures about boundedness remain open.
